purpose: Register OdontoForge as a shared transient-state / growth / EXIT operator connecting the JANUS-LAPIS regeneration lane and the Janus-Fundamentum P-vs-NP experimentation lane while preserving strict epistemic separation.

biological_regeneration.core_object: temporary repair state -> resolution EXIT -> stable tissue

computational_complexity.core_object: partial search state -> contradiction / regeneration / verified certificate
computational_complexity.evidence_authority: exact solver verification, proofs/certificates, preregistered benchmarks

operator_registry.role: preserve provenance and reusable operator vocabulary without promoting analogy to fact

odonto_vocabulary.INJECT_CHAOS: change search ordering/exploration under stagnation without changing truth conditions
odonto_vocabulary.regeneration: replace a failed state while preserving exactness/provenance

shared_measurement_layer.rule: Metric names may be shared; measurements and causal claims remain domain-specific.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer biological causality from OdontoForge behavior.
Do not infer P=NP or P!=NP from biological regeneration patterns.
Do not infer polynomial worst-case complexity from finite solver benchmarks.
Do not merge two domains solely because their diagrams look similar.
Do not promote a cross-domain mapping without a prospective prediction and domain-native validation.

complexity_boundary.required_for_complexity_claim: formal general proof under accepted definitions

next_tests: Run OdontoForge against preregistered hard SAT families and record exact transient-state lifetimes.
Compare Odonto branch-lifetime distributions with brute-force and conventional exact-search controls.
Keep the Lapis EXIT CLOCK independent and ask only whether the shared abstract metric yields prospective predictive value.
Preserve failed mappings as negative registry nodes.
